issues.failure_explanation: The only smallness condition imposed on the net scale is δ<τ_M/2 (through ε<(τ_M/2)^α; when L is small, δ^α≈ε). This does not make the radial factor ‖x−z_i‖/(pτ_M(z_i)) <1 for some i at every x∈M(q). Counterexample: M a circle of radius τ (local reach τ everywhere), q=0.9 so p=0.95, δ=0.49τ, a maximal separated net of 12 equispaced points (spacing 2πτ/12≈0.524τ>δ, maximal). Take v the arc-midpoint between two net points (arc distance ≈0.262τ) and x=v+u with u outward normal, ‖u‖→qτ. Then ‖x−z_i‖²/τ² = (1+q)²+1−2(1+q)cos(0.262)≈0.94, so ‖x−z_i‖≈0.969τ>0.95τ=pτ(z_i) for the two nearest net points and even more for all others. Hence η̃_i(x)=0 for all i, ‖η̃(x)‖₁=0 and η(x)=η̃(x)/‖η̃(x)‖₁ is undefined; the claimed lower bound 1−q≲‖η̃‖₁ and the localization/partition-of-unity properties invoked from Cloninger21 require δ to be small relative to (1−q)τ_M, a hypothesis absent from Theorem thmApprox and Proposition approxetai.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore, $\|\tilde\eta(x)\|_1$ is uniformly bounded above and bounded away from zero.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add an explicit hypothesis δ ≤ c(q)τ_M (equivalently restrict ε to (0, ε_0(q,τ_M,L,α))) matching the hypotheses under which Cloninger21 Prop. 6.3 gives 1−q ≲ ‖η̃‖₁, in both Theorem thmApprox and Proposition approxetai.
issues.overall_effect: For ε near the top of the admitted range (and q close to 1 or L small) the oracle approximator f̂ and the target η of Proposition approxetai are not defined, so the approximation guarantee is not established over the whole stated ε-range; the asymptotic (small ε) content is unaffected.
issues.title: Stated ε (i.e. δ<τ/2) range does not guarantee the partition of unity is well defined: ‖η̃(x)‖₁ can vanish on M(q)
issues.why_classification: A local strengthening of the admissible ε/δ range (constants already hidden in O(·) depend on q,τ_M) restores every claim, rate and scope for small ε; no new argument is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: Membership in the class 𝓣(…,R,κ) requires sup over all of ℝ^D of |T| to be at most R. The constructed network computes squares, products and a truncated power series of the input via ReLU attention whose identities (e.g. σ(x^i+M)=x^i+M) only hold for ‖x‖_∞ ≤ M; on ℝ^D its output is an unbounded polynomial-type function, and even on M(q) the proof only yields |T| ≤ ‖g‖_∞+ε, not ≤ R. No clipping step or verification of the R-bound appears. The bias step of Theorem thmGeneralization (inf over 𝓣 of ‖T−f‖_∞ ≤ O(ε)) and the use of Lemma 6 of Chen22 (which needs the class bounded by R) therefore rely on an unverified class membership.

issues.failure_explanation: For the truncation error |1−c‖η̃(x)‖₁|^{r+1} ≤ ε to hold uniformly, one needs r ≥ ln(1/ε)/ln(1/ρ) with ρ = sup_x|1−c‖η̃(x)‖₁|. With ‖η̃‖₁ ∈ [c₁,c₂], c₁≍(1−q), c₂≍d^{d/2}(1−q)^{−2d} (the paper's own bounds), the best ρ satisfies ln(1/ρ) ≍ c₁/c₂, so r ≍ (c₂/c₁) ln(1/ε) = d^{d/2}(1−q)^{−2d−1} ln(1/ε), not O(ln(1/ε)) with a d-free constant. Consequently L_{T₂} = O(ln r) = ln ln(1/ε) + (d/2) ln d + O(d ln(1/(1−q))), so the depth is O(d ln d + ln ln(1/ε)) with the O hiding q, whereas Proposition approxetai and Theorems thmApprox/thmGeneralization assert L_T = O(d + ln ln(·)) with the hidden constant independent of d.

issues.overall_effect: The stated depth bound and its declared parameter dependence (no d-dependence in the O(·) for L_T; r=O(ln(1/ε))) are not supported; the correct bound carries an extra d ln d term and the head count r carries a factor exponential in d (absorbed in m_T only because m_T's O(·) already hides d).
